## Hook (first 3 seconds)
**On-screen text:** "18 hours for one cup of coffee."
**Visual:** Close-up, sound-on — cold water dripping slowly through dark grounds, condensation on the glass. The drip is audible.
**VO:** "Eighteen hours for one glass of cold brew. Here's what that time actually buys you."

*Archetype: Specific Number. Structure: Myth/Correction — the belief is that slow brewing is just a flex; the correction is that time is doing chemical work.*

## Body (3-4 scenes with cues)

**Scene 1 — the villain (≈4s)**
**On-screen text:** "Bitterness = heat + speed"
**Visual:** Quick cut to a hot cup, steam rising fast.
**VO:** "Hot water pulls flavour fast — but it also drags out the bitter, acidic stuff. Speed is the problem."

**Scene 2 — the fix (≈4s)**
**On-screen text:** "Cold + slow leaves it behind"
**Visual:** Back to the slow drip, grounds swelling in cold water.
**VO:** "Cold water extracts gently. Over 18 hours it takes the sweetness and the chocolate notes — and leaves the bitterness in the grounds."

**Scene 3 — the proof (≈4s)**
**On-screen text:** "Smooth. Never sharp."
**Visual:** Pour over ice in one clean stream; first sip, no wince.
**VO:** "That's why it tastes round instead of sharp. No sugar hiding anything — just time."

## CTA
**Payoff line (before the ask):** "Eighteen hours. That's the whole secret."
**On-screen text:** "Send this to the friend who takes theirs black."
**VO:** "Send this to the person who swears all cold brew tastes bitter — this is the one that doesn't."

**Caption (first line):** Heat makes coffee bitter. Cold time makes it smooth — here's the chemistry.
